text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London fell in light trading, but bounced off support amid some industry price fixing at the lows. Both March and May lost $11 to close at $1,783 and $1,718 per tonne, respectively. In New York the coffee market reasserted the uptrend with May briefly pushing back over 200 cents/lb and settling just below that point. March added 9.75 cents/lb to close at 215.50 cents/lb, while May closed 9.50 cents/lb higher at 199.30 cents/lb.

Talk of further retail price hikes and speculative buying pushed prices higher. It is astonishing that talk of price hikes aided sentiment as it hurts consumption in the long-term. However, announced price rises could lead to consumers hoarding coffee and tighten the nearby structure even further, putting the roasters in an even more precarious position, traders said. They pointed out that roasters hiking prices is constructive because it shows they have to go along with the rise in prices.

UNITED STATES - Folgers released a statement confirming that it will raise the list price on its standard 13-ounce can by 15 cents immediately due to higher prices of green coffee on the world market. The increase, which brings the new price for a standard can to $2.86, comes only one week after a 45- cent increase in the price of Folgers' 13-ounce can of ground coffee took effect.

BRAZIL - Mauricio Assis, the head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry said that coffee production in 1997/98 is now estimated at 20 to 22 million bags which compares to the January estimate of 18 to 20 million bags. Brazil also indicated it would like to see stocks reduced to 5 to 6 million bags or slashed by more than half. This would be accomplished if the crop was really that small, but many analysts doubt that it will be only 20 to 22 million bags and regard 24 to 25 million bags a more realistic figure.

JAPAN - Japan imported 404,486 bags of coffee in December 1996, 36 percent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports in calendar year 1996 up to 5.619 million bags, 5.5 percent more than was imported the previous year but significantly below the 1994 figure of 6.040 million bags. Main suppliers of green coffee in 1996 were Brazil (1.117 vs 1.150 million bags), Colombia (1.175 vs 0.978 million bags) and Indonesia (1.025 vs 0.809 million bags).
